title: How Rainbows Form
description: The sky-shard of the crystal can only be reached by summoning a real rainbow. Learn nature's own dispersion trick.

content.value: A rainbow is dispersion happening in the sky. After rain, millions of tiny water droplets float in the air. Each droplet acts like a tiny prism, splitting sunlight into the seven colours of VIBGYOR.

You need:
☀️  Sunlight (bright)
💧  Water droplets in the air (just after rain)
👤  The Sun BEHIND you, rain in FRONT of you

Inside each droplet, sunlight bends (refracts) as it enters, reflects off the back of the droplet, and bends again as it leaves — spreading into colours. Millions of droplets together paint the giant arch we call a rainbow, always with red on the outside and violet on the inside.
The colours reach your eye only from droplets at a certain angle from the Sun, and that set of droplets forms a curve in the sky — which is why a rainbow is always an arch.
You can make your own rainbow on a sunny day: stand with your back to the Sun and spray a fine mist of water in front of you. The mist droplets disperse the light — instant rainbow!

Key Takeaway: A rainbow forms when sunlight is dispersed by water droplets acting as tiny prisms. It appears when the Sun is behind you and rain is in front, with red on the outside and violet on the inside.

quiz.question: In a rainbow, each tiny water droplet acts like a…
quiz.explain: Each droplet splits sunlight into its colours, just like a glass prism — that is dispersion.

quiz.question: To see a rainbow, the Sun should be…
options: in front of you, rain behind you
behind you, rain in front of you
quiz.explain: With the Sun behind you and rain in front, dispersed light from the droplets reaches your eyes as a rainbow.

quiz.question: In a rainbow, which colour appears on the OUTER edge?
quiz.explain: A rainbow has red on the outside and violet on the inside.
